definition: made or done without advance planning
example: We held an impromptu picnic after the clouds cleared.
note: Impromptu describes the lack of advance preparation, even when the result works well.
memory: Picture making a plan only when the moment arrives.

definition: not clearly fixed or specified
example: The meeting was postponed for an indefinite period.
note: Indefinite leaves a number, limit, or time unsettled; it does not necessarily mean endless.
memory: An indefinite date has no fixed place on the calendar.

definition: thick and strongly built
example: A stout wooden pole supported the heavy sign.
note: Here stout concerns thickness and strength, rather than courage or a kind of drink.
memory: Picture a thick pole that will not easily bend.

definition: large enough in amount or degree to be important
example: Restoring the old theater required considerable effort.
note: Considerable indicates a substantial amount; it does not mean thoughtful toward others.
memory: Considerable effort is enough effort to take seriously.

definition: to provide or supply something needed
example: The school will furnish all the equipment for the experiment.
note: Furnish can mean provide, even when no furniture is involved.
memory: Furnish evidence means supply evidence.

definition: the regular movement of animals from one region to another
example: Bird migration brings thousands of geese to the wetland each autumn.
note: Animal migration is movement between regions, often linked to seasons, feeding, or breeding.
memory: Picture birds following a seasonal route.

definition: the complete disappearance of a species
example: Protecting nesting sites can help prevent the extinction of a rare bird.
note: Extinction means no members of a species remain alive; a local decline alone is different.
memory: No living members remain.

definition: a person who studies plants and animals in their surroundings
example: The naturalist recorded the insects living beneath fallen logs.
note: A naturalist studies nature; the word does not simply name someone who likes being outdoors.
memory: Nature is the naturalist's subject.

definition: to formally tell someone about something
example: Please notify the librarian if you find the missing book.
note: To notify is to give someone information, often about an event or required action.
memory: A notification tells you something.

definition: relating to the national government in a system of shared national and regional powers
example: A federal agency manages the program across several states.
note: Federal identifies the national level of government within a federation, rather than a city office.
memory: Think of the national level in a federation.

definition: the line of earlier generations from which a person or living thing descends
example: The two dog breeds share a common ancestry.
note: Ancestry looks backward toward earlier generations; descendants come later.
memory: Trace the family tree backward.

definition: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
example: The owl is a predator that catches mice at night.
note: A predator obtains food by hunting prey; it is a feeding role rather than a size category.
memory: The predator hunts; the prey is hunted.

definition: a preserved remain or trace of an organism from the distant past
example: The fossil showed the outline of a leaf in the rock.
note: A fossil may be a body remain or a trace such as a footprint, not necessarily a complete skeleton.
memory: Picture a trace of ancient life preserved in rock.

definition: a scientist who studies ancient life through fossils
example: The paleontologist examined a tooth found in the cliff.
note: Paleontologists study ancient life; archaeologists study the human past through material remains.
memory: Fossils are clues for the paleontologist.

definition: a disagreement about a matter that people debate strongly
example: The proposed road caused controversy among local residents.
note: Controversy involves disagreement; it does not establish which side is correct.
memory: Picture opposing sides debating the same question.

definition: to look or be like someone or something
example: The moth's folded wings resemble a dry leaf.
note: Resemble expresses similarity, without claiming two things are identical.
memory: Similar features make one thing resemble another.

definition: impressively grand or dignified
example: The majestic mountain rose above the clouds.
note: Majestic describes an imposing appearance or dignity, rather than ordinary usefulness.
memory: Picture a mountain towering over the landscape.

definition: a small part left after most of something is gone
example: A remnant of the old wall stood beside the new road.
note: A remnant is what survives removal, destruction, or loss; it need not be a complete object.
memory: Most is gone; a remnant remains.

definition: an area of land under a particular control or occupation
example: The wolf pack defended its territory from other packs.
note: Territory is an area associated with control or occupation, not simply any scenic location.
memory: Picture the boundary of an area a group controls.

definition: to live in a place
example: Several kinds of frogs inhabit the marsh.
note: Inhabit takes the place directly: animals inhabit a forest, without needing the preposition in.
memory: A habitat is a place that organisms inhabit.

definition: originally occurring in a particular region
example: The garden contains only plants native to the region.
note: Native relates an organism to its original region; it does not mean merely common everywhere.
memory: Link a native species to its home region.

definition: to act against something in order to reduce its effect
example: The town planted trees to counter the effects of soil erosion.
note: Here counter is an action taken against a problem, rather than a shop surface or counting device.
memory: A countermeasure works against a threat.

definition: to measure and examine land in order to map or plan it
example: Engineers will survey the valley before designing the bridge.
note: Here survey means examining and measuring terrain, rather than asking people for opinions.
memory: A land survey comes before a route is planned.

definition: a long cloud or stream shaped like a feather
example: A plume of dust rose behind the truck.
note: A plume can be a feather-shaped cloud of dust, smoke, or vapor, rather than a bird's actual feather.
memory: Picture dust rising in a featherlike column.

definition: to remain suspended in the air above one place
example: A dragonfly seemed to hover above the pond.
note: Hover emphasizes remaining over an area, rather than traveling steadily onward.
memory: Picture staying in the air over one spot.

definition: to bend or give way under pressure
example: Extreme heat can cause a metal rail to buckle.
note: Here buckle means bend out of shape, rather than fasten a belt.
memory: Picture a straight strip bending under stress.

definition: falling or flowing rapidly in very large amounts
example: The torrential rain flooded the footpath within minutes.
note: Torrential describes powerful quantities of water, not just a few scattered drops.
memory: Think of water pouring in a torrent.

definition: deserving praise or approval
example: Her commendable honesty helped the team correct its mistake.
note: Commendable evaluates an action as worthy of praise; commend means to praise.
memory: An action you would commend is commendable.

definition: the protection and careful use of natural resources
example: Water conservation helped the town through the dry summer.
note: Conservation protects resources and avoids waste; it need not mean preventing all use.
memory: Conserve today so resources remain tomorrow.

definition: the reduction of a supply through use or loss
example: Repeated pumping caused the depletion of the underground water supply.
note: Depletion describes a supply becoming smaller, sometimes before it is completely exhausted.
memory: Picture the supply level falling.

definition: impossible to use up completely
example: The storyteller seemed to have an inexhaustible supply of ideas.
note: Inexhaustible means unable to be exhausted; a very large supply can still have limits.
memory: Inexhaustible is the opposite of able to run out.

definition: the presence of harmful substances or waste in the environment
example: The cleanup reduced pollution in the stream.
note: Pollution harms environmental quality; ordinary natural change is not automatically pollution.
memory: Picture harmful waste entering clean water.

definition: wood used or prepared for building
example: The workers stacked the timber beside the unfinished shed.
note: Timber names wood as a building resource, rather than an individual finished table or chair.
memory: Trees can supply building timber.

definition: a very large quantity of something
example: The orchard produced an abundance of apples this year.
note: Abundance means a plentiful supply; it is the noun related to abundant.
memory: Abundant describes; abundance names the plenty.

definition: to do something badly through mistakes or poor skill
example: Rushing may cause you to botch an otherwise simple repair.
note: Botch emphasizes a job done badly, rather than a plan merely delayed.
memory: A botched job needs to be put right.

definition: to determine a quantity or result by mathematical reasoning
example: We can calculate the area by multiplying length by width.
note: Calculate involves working out a result, rather than simply reporting a guess.
memory: Use known numbers to work out an unknown.

definition: the curved path of an object moving around another object in space
example: The satellite follows an orbit around Earth.
note: Orbit names the path, rather than the object traveling along it.
memory: Picture the path circling a planet.

definition: the attraction between objects that have mass
example: Earth's gravity pulls the dropped ball toward the ground.
note: Here gravity is a physical attraction, rather than seriousness of manner.
memory: A falling ball is a familiar clue to gravity.

definition: a scientist who studies objects and phenomena in space
example: The astronomer used a telescope to examine the distant star.
note: Astronomers study space; the word does not mean a person who travels there.
memory: The astronomer studies stars; the astronaut travels in space.

definition: information gained by carefully watching or measuring
example: Her observation of the nest helped explain the birds' behavior.
note: An observation records what is noticed or measured; an explanation interprets those findings.
memory: First observe a pattern, then try to explain it.

definition: a case that does not follow a general rule or pattern
example: Every shelf was empty, with the exception of the top one.
note: An exception falls outside a stated pattern; it does not necessarily disprove every part of it.
memory: One case stands apart from the usual rule.

definition: after a short time; soon
example: The rain stopped, and presently the children returned outside.
note: In older storytelling, presently often means soon afterward; it can mean currently in other contexts.
memory: In a story, picture the next event happening shortly.

definition: to require someone to do something because of a duty or circumstance
example: The blocked road may oblige us to take a longer route.
note: In be obliged to, a person is required or forced to act; it is different from doing a favor.
memory: Obliged to means having to.

definition: a person who is very interested in an activity or subject
example: A gardening enthusiast offered to help with the school greenhouse.
note: An enthusiast shows strong interest, without necessarily being a paid professional.
memory: Enthusiasm describes the enthusiast's interest.

definition: a person who takes part in an activity
example: Each participant received a map before the walking tour.
note: A participant takes part; a spectator mainly watches.
memory: Participate is the action; participant is the person.

definition: a person who lives in a particular place
example: A longtime resident explained how the neighborhood had changed.
note: A resident lives in a place, rather than merely visiting it.
memory: Residence is home to a resident.

definition: a residential community on the edge of or near a city
example: Their suburb has a train connection to the city center.
note: A suburb is connected to a larger city and is not simply any distant rural village.
memory: Picture a community near the city's edge.

definition: the collection of clothes a person owns
example: She added a warm coat to her winter wardrobe.
note: Here wardrobe means someone's clothes, rather than the cupboard used to store them.
memory: Picture all your clothes considered as one collection.

definition: intended to help people in need
example: The club organized a charitable sale to support the food bank.
note: Charitable describes help for others, rather than an activity done only for personal profit.
memory: A charity carries out charitable work.

definition: a general idea or principle
example: The model helped explain the concept of balance.
note: A concept is an idea that helps organize understanding; an example illustrates it.
memory: One concept can be illustrated by many examples.

definition: food or nourishment needed to support life
example: The small seeds provide sustenance for birds in winter.
note: Sustenance keeps a living thing alive; entertainment alone does not provide it.
memory: Sustain life with sustenance.

definition: a part attached to the main body of an animal or object
example: The crab used a jointed appendage to move food toward its mouth.
note: An appendage is attached to a main body, rather than being the whole organism.
memory: Picture a limb attached to a body.

definition: so small that a microscope is needed to see it clearly
example: The pond water contained microscopic organisms.
note: Microscopic concerns very small scale; it does not mean simply far away.
memory: A microscope makes microscopic things visible.

definition: a community of organisms and the physical environment with which they interact
example: The pond ecosystem includes insects, fish, plants, water, and soil.
note: An ecosystem includes both organisms and their physical surroundings, not just a list of animals.
memory: Living things plus their interacting environment.

definition: relating to the very deep regions of the ocean
example: Very little sunlight reaches the abyssal regions of the sea.
note: Abyssal identifies great ocean depth, rather than merely being underwater near a beach.
memory: Think of the deep ocean beyond sunlight.

definition: to cover or hide something from view
example: Thick fog can shroud the island before sunrise.
note: As a verb, shroud means conceal under a covering; it need not involve a burial cloth.
memory: Picture fog wrapping a hill and hiding it.

definition: to impress or amaze with brightness or beauty
example: The brilliant colors of the mural dazzle visitors.
note: Dazzle can describe an overwhelming visual impression, rather than explaining something logically.
memory: Picture brilliant color capturing your attention.

definition: to be full of living things
example: The tide pools teem with small crabs and snails.
note: Teem with emphasizes abundant life or activity; it does not mean merely contain one item.
memory: A pool that teems is alive with many creatures.

definition: sleep, especially peaceful sleep
example: The distant thunder did not disturb the baby's slumber.
note: Slumber is a literary word for sleep; plants may be described as sleeping figuratively.
memory: Picture a peaceful sleeper.

definition: unusually thin and weak-looking
example: The scrawny seedling needed better light and soil.
note: Scrawny suggests thinness with weakness or poor growth, rather than elegant slimness.
memory: Picture a thin, struggling seedling.

definition: to play and move about happily
example: The puppies frolic on the grass after their nap.
note: Frolic combines playful movement with enjoyment, rather than ordinary walking.
memory: Picture puppies leaping in play.

definition: in an unwilling or hesitant manner
example: He reluctantly left the playground when it was time to go.
note: Reluctantly describes how someone acts despite not wanting to do it.
memory: The action happens, but the person would rather avoid it.

definition: to fail to give needed care or attention to something
example: If we neglect the young plants, they may dry out.
note: Neglect concerns a lack of necessary care; deliberate destruction is a different action.
memory: Care is needed but not given.

definition: an established set of actions performed for a ceremony or tradition
example: Lighting the lanterns became a yearly ritual in the village.
note: A ritual follows an established pattern and often has symbolic meaning.
memory: Picture a ceremony performed in a familiar order.

definition: to officially forgive someone or release them from a punishment
example: The ruler agreed to pardon the prisoner after reviewing the case.
note: Pardon removes or forgives a penalty; it does not necessarily establish innocence.
memory: A pardon releases someone from punishment.

definition: to lead or be in charge of a meeting or ceremony
example: The principal will preside over the graduation ceremony.
note: Preside concerns leading proceedings, rather than merely attending them.
memory: The person at the chair presides.

definition: once every year
example: The town holds its harvest fair annually.
note: Annually specifies a yearly frequency; it does not mean every season.
memory: Annual events happen annually.

definition: the outside or uppermost layer of something
example: A leaf floated on the surface of the pond.
note: Here surface names the upper boundary of the water, rather than the action of coming up.
memory: Picture the boundary between water and air.

definition: a basic good or raw material that can be bought and sold
example: Wheat is an important commodity in many farming regions.
note: A commodity is a tradable good, often a basic material, rather than a service or opinion.
memory: Picture grain sold as a basic trade good.

definition: a food regularly eaten as a main part of a diet
example: Rice is a staple in many households.
note: Here staple means a basic dietary food, rather than the metal fastener used for paper.
memory: A dietary staple appears on the table regularly.

definition: so small in amount that it seems inadequate or unimportant
zh: 微不足道的；少得可怜的
example: The paltry payment barely covered the cost of the bus ride.
note: Paltry adds a judgment of insufficiency to small size or amount.
memory: Picture a payment too small to cover the need.

definition: showing great wealth and luxury
example: The opulent hall had marble floors and gilded ceilings.
note: Opulent stresses richness and luxury, rather than simple comfort.
memory: Picture a room overflowing with costly decoration.

definition: generally believed or said to be something
example: The reputed expert could not explain the simplest part of the machine.
note: Reputed marks what people say or believe, without guaranteeing that the reputation is deserved.
memory: A reputation is a report, not proof.

definition: something spoken aloud
example: Her brief utterance ended the long silence.
note: An utterance is a spoken expression; it need not be a long formal speech.
memory: To utter is to speak; an utterance is what is spoken.

definition: the period or consequences following a major and usually harmful event
example: Neighbors helped repair homes in the aftermath of the storm.
note: Aftermath focuses on what follows an event, especially its damaging consequences.
memory: Picture the cleanup after the storm.

definition: an invented story presented as though it were true
example: The witness admitted that the dramatic story was a fabrication.
note: Here fabrication means a made-up account, rather than the manufacture of an object.
memory: A fabricated account was invented, not observed.

definition: the mistaken crediting of words or work to the wrong source
example: The misattribution gave the poet credit for a line written by someone else.
note: Misattribution gives the wrong source credit; the words themselves may still be real.
memory: Real words can have the wrong name attached.

definition: a person who places excessive importance on minor rules or details
zh: 卖弄学问者；拘泥细节者
example: The pedant interrupted the story to correct a tiny error in the date.
note: Pedant is critical of excessive concern with details, rather than a neutral label for any careful scholar.
memory: Picture tiny corrections interrupting the main point.

definition: to shut away from ordinary social contact
example: The writer chose to cloister herself in a quiet cabin until the draft was finished.
note: Cloister as a verb stresses separation from outside life, rather than simply living in a particular room.
memory: Picture a retreat cut off from daily bustle.

definition: the act of putting something into something else
example: The insertion of a new paragraph made the explanation clearer.
note: Insertion is adding something inside an existing space or structure, rather than removing it.
memory: Insert means put in; insertion names the act.

definition: different in ways that combine well or complete one another
example: Their complementary skills made the project easier to finish.
note: Complementary things complete or balance each other; complimentary means praising or free of charge.
memory: Complementary skills complete a team.

definition: the process or system through which something works
example: The students investigated the mechanism that makes the toy move.
note: A mechanism explains how a result is produced, rather than merely naming the result.
memory: Ask how the parts or steps make it work.

definition: a system of ideas about life, knowledge, or how things should be understood
example: The school's philosophy emphasizes curiosity and careful reasoning.
note: Philosophy organizes broad ideas and principles; it is more than one passing opinion.
memory: Picture guiding ideas that fit into a system.

definition: a mammal belonging to the group that includes humans, apes, monkeys, and lemurs
example: A lemur is a primate with grasping hands and feet.
note: Primate names a biological group, rather than every tree-dwelling animal.
memory: Think of humans, apes, monkeys, and lemurs.

definition: an animal in the group whose females produce milk to feed their young
example: The whale is a mammal even though it lives in the sea.
note: Mammals are classified by biological traits, rather than by whether they live on land.
memory: Milk for the young is a key clue.

definition: opposite in meaning, direction, or effect
example: The two witnesses gave contrary accounts of the same event.
note: In contrary to, the meaning is opposed to, rather than in support of.
memory: Contrary evidence points the other way.

definition: to tell or command someone to do something
example: The old tale says the queen would bid her guards open the gate.
note: In older writing, bid can mean command; bade and bidden are related past forms.
memory: A queen's bidding is her command.

definition: a sheltered area of water where ships can stay safely
example: The fishing boats returned to the harbor before the storm.
note: A harbor shelters boats; it is a place rather than a particular vessel.
memory: Picture boats sheltered behind a breakwater.

definition: a large branch of a tree
example: Snow collected on the lowest bough of the oak.
note: A bough is a main tree branch, rather than a tiny twig or the tree's trunk.
memory: Picture a thick branch extending from the trunk.

definition: a color or shade of color
example: The sunset gave the clouds a rosy hue.
note: Hue identifies color, rather than an object's shape or texture.
memory: Ask which color you see.

definition: subdued or restrained in color or style
example: The room's sober colors suited the quiet memorial.
note: Here sober describes restrained coloring, rather than whether someone has consumed alcohol.
memory: Picture muted colors in a quiet room.

definition: the process of building again after damage or destruction
example: The reconstruction of the bridge took two years after the flood.
note: Reconstruction builds again; it is different from constructing something for the first time.
memory: Re- adds the idea of again.

definition: the condition of remaining steady and unlikely to change or collapse
example: Extra supports improved the stability of the platform.
note: Stability is steadiness in a structure or situation, rather than rapid growth.
memory: A stable structure has stability.

definition: joined into a single coordinated whole
example: The groups presented a unified plan for cleaning the park.
note: Unified means brought together, without requiring every member to be identical.
memory: Many parts work as one whole.

definition: help or support given to someone
example: The hikers needed assistance to move the fallen branch.
note: Assistance names the help provided; assistant names a person who helps.
memory: Assist is the action; assistance is the help.

definition: plain and striking, with little decoration or softness
example: The photograph captured the stark beauty of the treeless hillside.
note: Stark can describe a bare yet striking appearance, rather than rich decoration.
memory: Picture a bare hillside with clear, strong outlines.

definition: introducing new ideas or methods that others may later follow
example: Her pioneering design changed how later bridges were built.
note: Pioneering concerns leading the way in a field, not merely copying an established method.
memory: A pioneer opens a path for others.

definition: to show or represent something in words or pictures
example: The painting will depict the town as it looked a century ago.
note: Depict means represent; it does not guarantee a completely realistic or literal treatment.
memory: A depiction shows a subject.

definition: represented as more perfect than it is in reality
example: The poster showed an idealized village without traffic or litter.
note: Idealized describes a polished representation, rather than proof that the subject is perfect.
memory: Picture reality with its flaws removed.

definition: showing recognizable subjects through simplified or partly abstract forms
example: The semiabstract painting suggested a flower through a few curved shapes.
note: Semiabstract art keeps some recognizable features while simplifying others.
memory: Semi- means partly: partly abstract, partly recognizable.

definition: relating to places where people live
example: The new rules limit loud construction in residential streets.
note: Residential concerns homes and their areas, rather than factories or commercial offices.
memory: Residents live in residential areas.

definition: an organized series of actions intended to reach a goal
example: The class began a campaign to reduce paper waste.
note: A campaign is sustained, organized effort; it need not involve an election or a war.
memory: Many coordinated actions work toward one goal.

definition: with people or things considered or acting together
example: The classes collectively collected enough books to fill the library shelf.
note: Collectively emphasizes the combined group, rather than each person's separate result.
memory: Collect the separate efforts into one group result.

definition: to give less attention or importance to something than it deserves
example: A short report may underemphasize the difficulties faced by volunteers.
note: Underemphasize means give too little weight, rather than say nothing at all.
memory: Under- means too little emphasis.

definition: a person who controls or runs a machine or system
example: The operator checked the controls before starting the machine.
note: An operator runs equipment; the word does not automatically mean its inventor or owner.
memory: Operate is the action; operator is the person.

definition: a machine or frame used for weaving cloth
example: The weaver stretched threads across the loom.
note: Here loom is a noun naming equipment, rather than a verb meaning appear threateningly.
memory: The loom is the weaver's tool.

definition: made or produced by people rather than occurring naturally
example: The greenhouse used artificial light during the short winter days.
note: Artificial describes origin, not necessarily poor quality or deliberate deception.
memory: A lamp supplies artificial light.

definition: light that makes an area or object visible
example: The reading lamp provided enough illumination for the desk.
note: Illumination here is physical lighting, rather than a new understanding of an idea.
memory: Illuminate means light up.

definition: a narrow connecting passage or route
example: A corridor of protected woodland links the two forests.
note: A corridor can be an ecological route, as well as a hallway inside a building.
memory: Picture a narrow connection between larger areas.

definition: to move in a curve that winds around a center
example: We watched a paper seed spiral toward the ground.
note: Spiral movement winds around a center while changing distance or height.
memory: Picture a coiling path rather than a straight line.

definition: to watch or check something over time
example: The students will monitor the pond's water level each week.
note: Monitor means continue checking for change, rather than make only one observation.
memory: Repeated checks reveal a trend.

definition: to protect or screen something from exposure or harm
example: A shade can shield the window from the afternoon sun.
note: Shield can mean block exposure with a cover, as well as defend against a physical attack.
memory: Picture a cover between the object and the exposure.

definition: one framed picture in a sequence in a comic
example: The final panel shows the cyclist arriving home.
note: In comics, a panel is one picture unit; several panels build a sequence.
memory: One comic picture fits inside one panel.

definition: the blank space separating panels in a comic
example: The gutter separates the two drawings without showing every moment between them.
note: Here gutter means the blank between comic panels, rather than a channel that carries rainwater.
memory: The reader bridges the blank between pictures.

definition: a nest or structure in which a colony of bees lives
example: The bees returned to the hive carrying pollen.
note: A hive is the colony's home, rather than one bee or one drop of honey.
memory: Many bees share one hive.

definition: to make something previously hidden or unclear known or visible
example: The falling water level began to reveal the stones beneath.
note: Reveal brings something into view or understanding, rather than creating it from nothing.
memory: A hidden pattern becomes visible.

definition: having thin, irregular lines like a spider's legs
zh: 细长弯曲的；像蜘蛛腿的
example: The old letter was covered in spidery handwriting.
note: Spidery compares the shape of lines to spider legs; it does not claim that a spider wrote them.
memory: Picture thin handwriting spreading like spider legs.

definition: to gradually lose color, strength, or clarity
example: Sunlight can cause the ink to fade over time.
note: Fade is a gradual weakening, rather than something disappearing all at once.
memory: Picture ink growing paler year after year.

definition: an official document giving permission to do something
example: The hikers obtained a permit before camping in the reserve.
note: Here permit is a noun naming authorization; as a verb it can mean allow.
memory: A permit is paper proof of permission.

definition: a firm container used for holding or storing something
example: We kept the flour in a sealed canister.
note: A canister is a container, not the food or equipment stored inside it.
memory: Picture a firm container with a lid.

definition: a number representing an amount or measurement
example: The report included a figure for the number of daily visitors.
note: Here figure means a numerical value, rather than a shape, person, or drawing.
memory: A column of figures is a column of numbers.

definition: the pupa stage or outer case of a butterfly during its transformation
example: The chrysalis hung beneath the branch until the butterfly emerged.
note: A chrysalis is the butterfly's pupal stage or case, rather than a silk cocoon spun around it.
memory: Caterpillar, chrysalis, then butterfly.

definition: one of the sensory feelers on an insect's head
example: The insect moved one antenna toward the drop of nectar.
note: Here antenna is a biological sensory part, rather than equipment for receiving radio signals.
memory: An insect senses with its antennae.

definition: any one of the numerals from zero to nine
example: The final digit of the code is seven.
note: A digit is one numeral; a multi-digit number contains several of them.
memory: Three symbols make a three-digit number.

definition: a worker who keeps records or performs routine office tasks
example: The clerk checked the address before sorting the mail.
note: A clerk handles routine records or transactions; the job is different from directing the whole organization.
memory: Picture careful sorting and record keeping.

definition: something that makes a task easier or saves effort
example: The online map was a convenience for visitors planning their route.
note: A convenience makes life easier; it may be useful without being essential.
memory: Convenient describes; convenience names the help.

definition: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
example: Each inhabitant of the island depended on the ferry service.
note: Inhabitant names a living occupant; inhabit is the verb for living there.
memory: Those who inhabit a place are its inhabitants.

definition: organized resistance against a government or other authority
example: The rebellion began when the ruler refused to hear the people's demands.
note: Rebellion is resistance to authority, rather than ordinary disagreement between equals.
memory: Picture an uprising against those in power.

definition: to have one's home in a place
example: Many of the artists reside near the old harbor.
note: Reside is a formal word for live in a place; a brief visit need not be residence.
memory: A resident resides in a residence.

definition: an area of land set aside for a particular purpose or community
example: The map marked the boundary of the reservation.
note: Here reservation names land, rather than a booking or a doubt about a proposal.
memory: Reserve can mean set aside; this sense names land set aside.

definition: extremely hot or burning
example: The searing afternoon heat drove the hikers into the shade.
note: Searing heat is intense enough to suggest burning, rather than merely mild warmth.
memory: Picture heat that feels as if it burns.

definition: scattered loosely over an area
example: The path was strewn with fallen leaves.
note: Strewn describes things spread about irregularly, rather than arranged in tidy rows.
memory: Picture leaves scattered across a path.

definition: height above sea level or another stated reference point
example: The air became cooler as the climbers gained altitude.
note: Altitude measures height, rather than distance traveled along the ground.
memory: Higher elevation means greater altitude.

definition: a very large number of people or things
example: A multitude of stars appeared above the dark valley.
note: Multitude stresses a large number, without specifying an exact count.
memory: Picture more items than you can quickly count.

definition: a formal event performed according to an established pattern
example: The awards ceremony began with a welcome from the principal.
note: A ceremony is a formal occasion; a ritual can be one repeated action within it.
memory: Picture a formal event with planned proceedings.

definition: strikingly impressive or dramatic to see
example: The fireworks created a spectacular display above the lake.
note: Spectacular emphasizes visual or dramatic impact, rather than quiet usefulness.
memory: A spectacle is an impressive sight.

definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
example: The architect will incorporate a reading corner into the library design.
note: Incorporate means make something part of a whole, rather than leave it separate beside it.
memory: Picture adding a part into the larger design.

definition: the state of being kept confined rather than living freely
example: The rescued turtle lived in captivity while its injury healed.
note: Captivity concerns restricted freedom; it does not by itself describe whether care is good or poor.
memory: Contrast a kept animal with one living freely.

definition: to keep within particular limits or boundaries
example: The temporary fence will confine the animals to one field.
note: Confine limits movement or range; it does not always mean putting someone in prison.
memory: Picture a boundary that cannot be crossed.

definition: a range containing different degrees or kinds of something
example: The survey recorded a broad spectrum of opinions.
note: Spectrum can mean a whole range, rather than only the colors produced by light.
memory: Picture different positions along one range.

definition: open to doubt about truth, reliability, or acceptability
example: The report's questionable figures needed checking before publication.
note: Questionable invites doubt or checking; it does not automatically mean proved false.
memory: A questionable claim still needs verification.

definition: extremely peaceful, pleasant, and seemingly perfect
zh: 田园诗般的；恬静美好的
example: They spent an idyllic afternoon beside the quiet lake.
note: Idyllic describes a peaceful ideal of happiness, especially in a place or experience.
memory: Picture a calm afternoon that seems perfect.

definition: relating to business or the sale of goods and services
example: The harbor serves both fishing boats and commercial ships.
note: Commercial concerns business activity; it does not mean that something is automatically successful.
memory: Commerce is trade; commercial activity involves business.

definition: a member of one's family
example: A distant relation sent us a photograph from the family archive.
note: In family contexts, a relation is a relative, rather than a connection between two ideas.
memory: Family relations are people related to you.

definition: a naturally occurring inorganic solid with a characteristic structure and composition
example: Quartz is a mineral found in many kinds of rock.
note: A mineral is a particular natural solid; a rock may contain several minerals.
memory: A rock can be made of several mineral ingredients.

definition: a mollusk with a shell made of two hinged parts
example: The clam is a bivalve that can close its shell tightly.
note: Bivalve refers to two shell parts, rather than two separate animals sharing a shell.
memory: Bi- means two: picture two joined shell halves.

definition: to join parts so that they can swing open and closed
example: The builder will hinge the lid to the back of the box.
note: To hinge parts is to connect them at a moving joint, rather than glue them rigidly together.
memory: Picture a door turning on its hinges.

definition: wrong or out of its proper place
example: The unusual silence suggested that something was amiss.
note: Amiss points to something wrong or out of order, rather than specifying exactly what the problem is.
memory: Something feels out of place.

definition: the act of taking part in an activity
example: The coach encouraged participation from every student.
note: Participation is taking part, rather than simply watching or knowing about an event.
memory: Participants show participation by joining in.

definition: to recognize the value or good qualities of something
example: After the long walk, we began to appreciate the comfort of a warm room.
note: Appreciate means recognize worth; it can involve gratitude without requiring a spoken thank-you.
memory: Notice the value of something you might overlook.

definition: unfavorable or dangerous to life or comfort
example: The hostile environment made it difficult for the plants to survive.
note: A hostile environment has difficult or harmful conditions; it need not have feelings or intend to attack.
memory: Picture conditions that work against survival.

definition: to take turns or occur one after the other repeatedly
example: The two students alternate as discussion leader each week.
note: As a verb, alternate describes taking turns; the adjective can describe every other item or occasion.
memory: A then B, then A again.

definition: an organism that comes from an earlier ancestral organism or group
example: The bird is a descendant of an earlier animal lineage.
note: In biology, descendant applies to organisms and evolutionary lineages, rather than only a human family tree.
memory: Ancestry looks backward; descendants come later.

definition: to come up to the top of a body of water
example: The swimmer had to surface for a breath.
note: As a verb, surface names movement toward the top; as a noun, it names the outer boundary itself.
memory: Move up until you reach the water surface.

definition: a long work surface where customers are served
example: She placed the coins on the counter beside the cash register.
note: Here counter is a shop surface, rather than the verb meaning oppose or a device that counts.
memory: Picture the surface between a customer and a server.

definition: a flat section forming part of a larger surface or structure
example: A glass panel allowed visitors to see inside the hive.
note: This sense names a physical section of a surface, rather than one picture in a comic sequence.
memory: Picture one flat section in a wall or window.

definition: a visible shape or pattern
example: The skater traced a looping figure on the ice.
note: Here figure is a shape or movement pattern, rather than a number in a report.
memory: Picture a loop drawn by a moving skater.
